gaps.sentence: He stopped ___ coffee before bed and now sleeps much better.
gaps.explanation: 'Stop doing' = quit the activity; 'stop to drink' would mean pause in order to drink.

gaps.sentence: She couldn't resist ___ the last biscuit.

gaps.explanation: bother + -ing (or to-infinitive): don't bother going. Both accepted.
deny + -ing or having + past participle: denied doing/having done. Both accepted.
too + adjective + to-infinitive: too young to stay.

gaps.sentence: I didn't mean ___ you — it was a joke.
gaps.explanation: mean (= intend) takes the to-infinitive: didn't mean to upset. (mean + -ing = involve.)

gaps.sentence: We can't risk ___ the deadline again.
The witness claims ___ the getaway car parked outside for an hour.
gaps.explanation: 'Claims to have seen' — the perfect infinitive marks an earlier action.
